slides.title: How Is a Tooth Structured?
bullets: Crown — the part visible in the oral cavity
Root — the part located within the jawbone
The boundary between crown and root — the neck (cervix) of the tooth
slides.caption: External view

slides.title: Enamel
bullets: The outer layer covering the crown
The hardest mineralized tissue in the human body
Contains no living cells, so it cannot regenerate on its own
slides.caption: Outer white layer in section

slides.title: Dentin
bullets: Forms the bulk of the tooth
Lies beneath the enamel and cementum
Contains fine dentinal tubules, which is why sensitivity can occur
slides.caption: Yellowish-white layer beneath the enamel

slides.title: Pulp
bullets: Soft tissue at the center of the tooth
Contains blood vessels and nerve fibers
Nourishes the tooth and provides sensation
slides.caption: Red central part

slides.title: Cementum and Root
bullets: Cementum covers the root surface
Periodontal ligament fibers attach to the cementum
The root canal extends the pulp tissue to the root apex

slides.title: Key Points
bullets: Enamel protects
Dentin is the main supporting tissue
Pulp is living tissue
Cementum attaches the root to the ligament

quiz.q: Which is the outer layer of the crown?
quiz.explanation: Enamel covers the crown and is the hardest tissue.

quiz.q: Where are blood vessels and nerves located?
quiz.explanation: The pulp is the soft, living tissue of the tooth.

quiz.q: To which layer do the periodontal ligament fibers attach?
quiz.explanation: The ligament fibers are anchored in root cementum.
Dentin lies beneath the enamel and cementum, surrounding the pulp.
